title: Modules & Tooling
description: Using try-catch blocks to handle errors gracefully.

lessons.title: What are JavaScript Modules?
lessons.content: Modules help organize code by splitting it into reusable pieces, allowing better maintainability and avoiding pollution of the global scope.

lessons.title: Exporting and Importing Modules
Default Exports
Why Use Modules?
lessons.content: Modules enable better code organization, help avoid naming conflicts, and support code reuse across different parts of an application or projects.

lessons.title: Introduction to Bundlers and Tooling
lessons.content: Tools like Webpack, Rollup, and Parcel bundle JavaScript modules and assets into optimized files for production, improving load times and developer experience.

lessons.title: Setting Up a Simple Module
Error Handling with try-catch
lessons.content: Try-catch blocks allow you to handle errors gracefully by catching exceptions and defining fallback behaviors, preventing your program from crashing unexpectedly.

lessons.title: Using try-catch Example
Modules in Node.js vs Browser
lessons.content: Node.js uses CommonJS modules by default (`require`/`module.exports`), while modern browsers support ES modules (`import`/`export`) for modular JavaScript.

lessons.title: Using Module Tooling in Projects
lessons.content: Setting up module bundlers and task runners in your workflow automates tasks like code transpiling, bundling, and live-reloading, boosting development efficiency.
